name: Omnara

modes.label: Managed machines
modes.note: Published tariff is memory-only: "$0.0414 per GiB of memory per hour online" (omnara.com/pricing, 2026-09-28); CPU is not billed separately (vcpu_h 0). vCPU per GiB and machine sizes are NOT published (create-machine API has no size fields), so the vCPU count of a priced shape is unverified. Retention "$0.20016 per GiB of memory per 30 days retained, in addition to runtime" is per GiB of machine memory, not per GiB of state, so it is not mapped to snapshot_gib_month.

caveats: Priced (fix 2026-09-28) on the published memory-hour rate only ($0.0414/GiB-h, CPU not billed separately). vCPU allocation per GiB is unpublished: a 4 vCPU request is NOT guaranteed. Retention of sleeping machines ($0.20016/GiB memory/30 days) is not included in the estimate.
Runtime $0.0414 per GiB memory-hour online. Retention $0.20016 per GiB MEMORY per 30 days, not disk GiB. CPU capacity-to-memory mapping unverified.
Idle sleep preserves data and pauses runtime; retaining machine still costs. BYO models/machines and Apache-2.0 self-hosting have $0 platform fee, but own compute/model bills remain.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Omnara Cloud is prepaid: managed sandboxes and managed models consume credits bought through Stripe; purchased credits are non-refundable; agents pause or fail when the organization has insufficient credits. Minimum purchase and any signup credit are not published ('No credit card required' to start).

Omnara is an agent control plane; its machines are sandboxes from Blaxel, Unikraft Cloud, Daytona or Modal. The provider, isolation and vCPU/RAM shape behind the Omnara-managed 'default-pool' are unpublished. With a BYO provider pool the compute is billed by that provider, not Omnara (Omnara platform fee $0).

Retention is charged 'in addition to runtime' for every retained machine (not only sleeping ones): while online the effective rate is $0.0414 + ~$0.000278 per GiB-hour. Pool machines are deleted after a configurable idle period (minimum 5 min; 0 disables), after which retention stops.

fleet.verification: No credit card for open-source self-hosting; hosted/Enterprise onboarding not specified.
fleet.tiers: Per agent: 1 machine by default ('By default, Omnara creates one machine at launch and allows one machine in total'), raised via max_machines within pool/project limits. Account-level limits of the hosted default-pool are unpublished.
fleet.notes: Current pricing offers open-source self-hosting and Enterprise deployment/on-prem support. No managed new-account VM quota established; customer-supplied infrastructure is not unlimited hosted fleet access.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A pool machine keeps its files, installed dependencies, and running processes across turns, including when the provider suspends and resumes it while idle.
snapshot_auto.note: Pricing page: 'Idle machines auto-sleep, preserving data and pausing runtime charges.' Trigger = idle; running processes (memory) preserved. Mechanism is the underlying provider's suspend (Blaxel / Unikraft Cloud / Daytona / Modal); Modal pool machines hard-terminate at 24 h. Pool machines are deleted after the configured idle-deletion period; replacements start from the pool image/snapshot.

own_agent_api.quote: Omnara is an open source platform for running managed agents. It handles execution and state while you choose the models, tools, machines, and how users interact with each agent.
own_agent_api.note: Omnara's OWN agent harness only (not Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode). REST API, TypeScript SDK, CLI and MCP server: launch agent from YAML config, POST inputs (follow-ups, steering), SSE event stream with resume, approvals, cron triggers, webhooks. The agent loop runs in Omnara's control plane, not inside the machine; machines (omnarad daemon) are attached as tool execution environments.

harness_api.quote: Omnara is an open source platform for running managed agents. It handles execution and state while you choose the models, tools, machines, and how users interact with each agent.
harness_api.note: Omnara's OWN agent harness only (not Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode). REST API, TypeScript SDK, CLI and MCP server: launch agent from YAML config, POST inputs (follow-ups, steering), SSE event stream with resume, approvals, cron triggers, webhooks. The agent loop runs in Omnara's control plane, not inside the machine; machines (omnarad daemon) are attached as tool execution environments.

secret_proxy.quote: secret_env_overlay references secrets, whose values are resolved when they are injected. Both apply to every process the agent runs on the machine
secret_proxy.note: Machine-side secrets are injected as env vars. Model-provider keys and MCP/OAuth tokens are used by the control-plane agent loop and never need to be on the machine, but there is no proxy for the machine's own outbound HTTP.

image_oci.note: Custom pool machines (BYO provider pools on Blaxel/Daytona/Modal/Unikraft) start from a user-specified image or snapshot. Not available for the default Omnara-managed pool, which uses a fixed environment.

desktop.quote: Omnara is an open source platform for running managed agents. It handles execution and state while you choose the models, tools, machines, and how users interact with each agent.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Omnara is a text/API agent control plane (run_command, file, and web tools) with no VNC/RDP/stream desktop offering documented anywhere in the docs.

browser.quote: web_fetch: Fetches a public HTTP or HTTPS URL and returns readable content as Markdown or plain text. It cannot access localhost or private networks.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the only web capability is a read-only fetch/search tool that returns text, not a real managed browser.

computer_use.quote: Omnara includes built-in tools for common agent tasks. ... run_command, read_process, write_process, stop_process, list_processes ...
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no screenshot/click computer-use API exists; tools are shell/process/file/web-search only.

anti_bot.quote: Omnara is the open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents. Run durable AI agents with any compatible model, tools, sandboxes, and approvals.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Omnara has no browser product, so stealth/fingerprint-evasion is not applicable.

captcha_solving.quote: Omnara is the open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents. Run durable AI agents with any compatible model, tools, sandboxes, and approvals.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser/CAPTCHA feature is documented.

ssh.quote: Every machine runs the same small daemon, omnarad, which connects outbound to the control plane. You do not need to open inbound ports, distribute SSH keys, or give Omnara a network path into your infrastructure.
ssh.note: Access to machines is exclusively via the omnarad daemon and run_command/process tools; no SSH access is documented or needed.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A replacement starts from the pool's original image or snapshot.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No user-triggered snapshot/checkpoint API exists in the API reference (no 'snapshot' endpoint group). Pool machines only preserve state automatically on provider-managed idle-suspend; the 'snapshot' referenced is the pool's fixed starting image, not an on-demand user checkpoint.

fork.note: create_machine provisions a new machine from the pool's configured image/snapshot; there is no operation to clone an existing machine's current state into a new one.

fork_running.note: No clone-while-running capability is documented; create_machine only adds a fresh pool machine from the base image/snapshot.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork capability at all is documented, so a memory-preserving fork is not offered.

wake_on_request.quote: A machine is available to an agent only when its binding is attached, its project grant still exists, its lifecycle is active, and its daemon is online or the machine is asleep and can be woken.
wake_on_request.note: Machines that are 'asleep' can be woken to serve a tool call; the underlying provider's suspend/resume is what Omnara relies on for idle pool machines.

volume_attach.note: Pool configuration exposes image/region/memory/CPU only; no attachable extra-volume feature is documented. The mounted-storage example attaches storage only via a user-run FUSE mount inside a BYO machine, not a provider-managed volume.

volume_shared.quote: A Docker container runs the Omnara daemon next to an rclone FUSE mount, and the agent uses that mount as its working directory.
volume_shared.note: No provider-managed shared-volume feature across multiple running machines is documented; only a single BYO machine's own FUSE mount is shown.

live_resize.quote: Size machines per call: When an agent creates a machine, it can request CPU and memory for that machine, where the provider supports it, within your pool and project limits.
live_resize.note: Sizing is set only at machine-creation time (per create_machine call); there is no documented way to resize a machine's CPU/RAM while it is running.

agent_harnesses.quote: Omnara is an open source platform for running managed agents. It handles execution and state while you choose the models, tools, machines, and how users interact with each agent.
agent_harnesses.note: Omnara runs its own agent loop in the control plane against any model you configure; it does not offer preinstalled third-party coding harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode as templates.

public_ipv4.quote: You do not need to open inbound ports, distribute SSH keys, or give Omnara a network path into your infrastructure.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the architecture is outbound-only (daemon dials the control plane); no public IPv4 per machine is documented.

inbound_https.quote: You do not need to open inbound ports, distribute SSH keys, or give Omnara a network path into your infrastructure.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no feature exposes machine ports as HTTPS URLs; all access is agent tool calls over the daemon's outbound connection.

ingress_rules.quote: You do not need to open inbound ports, distribute SSH keys, or give Omnara a network path into your infrastructure.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no inbound path to machines at all, so no ingress-control feature is needed or documented.

gpu.quote: default_machine_memory_mb, min_machine_memory_mb, max_machine_memory_mb ... machine_cpu and machine_memory_mb set the default size
gpu.note: Pool sizing options documented are limited to CPU and memory; no GPU machine type or option is mentioned anywhere in the docs or pricing page.

windows.quote: Omnara-managed machines, billed for storage and active time
windows.note: The card's managed-machine mode is Linux-only (Omnara-managed pool machines come from Blaxel/Unikraft/Daytona/Modal, all Linux sandboxes); run_command's pwsh/cmd shell options apply only to a user's own BYO Windows computer, which is not an Omnara-offered machine type.

macos.quote: Omnara-managed machines, billed for storage and active time
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS managed machine type is offered; BYO lets you connect any computer you already own, but that is not a provided macOS product.

eu_data_residency.quote: Omnara maintains a comprehensive security and compliance program to protect customer data across our North American operations.
eu_data_residency.note: The Trust Center explicitly scopes data protection to North American operations, with no EU region option documented.
